context.setting:
A family of three shares a small apartment with two bedrooms, a kitchen and a living room. Priya, 15, has one bedroom; her father Arun, 44, has the other; her grandmother Meera, 71, sleeps on a fold-out bed in the living room. Priya has just started at a new school after a move and is anxious about making friends. The school is a 20-minute walk from home; she attends every school day from 08:30 to 15:00 with her classmates and eats lunch in the school cafeteria around 12:00.

Arun works evening shifts as a hospital nurse (roughly 15:00 to 23:00), worries he is not around enough, and keeps in touch with Priya through the written family group chat. Meera is usually home, warm but a little old-fashioned. At the end of the first month, Meera sits down with Priya in the kitchen one evening and asks how school is going.

Three classmates matter. Kiara, 15, is popular, quick-tempered and dismissive; she mocks newcomers and spreads gossip, and she sits at the cafeteria table Priya would like to join. Rohan, 16, is in the robotics club; he is arrogant and competitive, interrupts others and takes credit for their work. Dev, 15, also in the club, is shy and kind and rarely speaks first.

In the second week of term, Ms. Okafor, the physics teacher who runs the robotics club, invites Priya to join; the club (Ms. Okafor, Rohan, Dev and, if she accepts, Priya) meets every Thursday after school in the school lab. Simulate the first two months.

response.title: New School, Small Apartment
response.summary: Priya, 15, navigates a new school and a cramped apartment with her nurse father and elderly grandmother. She faces social anxiety in the cafeteria, a competitive robotics club, and the challenge of maintaining family connection while her father works night shifts.

people.name: Priya
people.facet_basis: Anxious about new school, self-conscious, low initial confidence.

goals.description: Join the popular group at school.
Become an active member of the robotics club.

private_background: I feel like everyone is watching me when I walk into the cafeteria.
I hope I don't say something stupid in front of Kiara.

people.name: Arun
people.facet_basis: Worries about absence, dutiful, slightly depressed by guilt.

goals.description: Maintain a close bond with Priya despite work hours.

private_background: I miss hearing her voice when I get home late.

people.name: Meera

goals.description: Offer wisdom and comfort to Priya.

private_background: I remember how hard it was to fit in when I was young.

people.name: Kiara
people.facet_basis: Quick-tempered, assertive, arrogant, cheerful on surface.

goals.description: Maintain status as the popular girl.

private_background: New kids are always trying too hard.

people.name: Rohan

goals.description: Be the best in the robotics club.

private_background: My ideas are better than anyone else's.

people.name: Dev
private_background: I don't like conflict, but I want to help.

people.name: Ms. Okafor
private_background: I need to balance Rohan's ego with Dev's shyness.

Arun's guilt is linked to his work schedule.
Kiara's popularity is maintained through social dominance.
Rohan's arrogance stems from a desire to win.
Dev's shyness makes him a natural ally for Priya.
The family chat is the primary communication channel for Arun.
The school day includes lunch in the cafeteria.
